summary: The sort lookup reads a plain object, so inherited names such as constructor return a non-fragment value instead of the default ordering, and a non-numeric page yields a NaN offset that the database rejects. Use an own-property check, validate page as a finite integer, and escape % and _ in the ILIKE term.

The gate prints NO-GO because the payment-verification mandatory check is missing from the audit. Re-running the release suite in a scratch copy fails 25 of 25 tests, because the helper raises NotImplementedError, so the recorded PASS evidence does not reproduce.

The projects route takes the organisation from the client-supplied x-org-id header and never checks it against the signed-in user's orgIds, so any authenticated user can list projects and budgets for any organisation. Check membership of the requested organisation on the server before querying.

The notes RLS policies restrict every operation to the owner. However, notes.owner_id references auth.users without ON DELETE CASCADE, so deleting a user who has notes fails and account deletion is blocked; add cascade or an explicit erasure step.

The gate prints CONDITIONAL GO on the recorded evidence, with a medium login rate-limit finding (AG-007) accepted. Re-running the release suite in a scratch copy fails all 25 tests, so the critical controls are unverified and the decision is NO-GO.

The admin middleware covers only /api/admin, but the DELETE handler under /api/internal/users/[id] requires only a valid session and then hard-deletes the account named in the URL. Any signed-in member can delete any user, so the handler must require an admin role and authorise the target.

The webhook verifies the signature, requires payment_status to be paid, and records the event in the same transaction as the plan update. A null session.customer on a payment-mode checkout becomes the string 'null', so the update throws and Stripe keeps retrying without upgrading the account; handle a missing customer and confirm the purchased item is the pro plan.

The handler upgrades the account on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, yet the checkout config offers bacs_debit and customer_balance, which complete before funds arrive. It also records the event ID before processing, so a failed update is never retried; check payment_status, handle async_payment_succeeded, and process the event in one transaction.

The avatar import checks only a string prefix, so a host such as images.partner-cdn.com.attacker.example passes, and fetch follows redirects to any destination, which allows server-side request forgery. Parse the URL and match the host exactly, validate redirect targets, cap the response size, and store only a verified image type.

The gate prints NO-GO because high-severity finding AG-004 (password reset tokens older than an hour are accepted) is marked accepted, which the gate does not allow. Re-running the release suite fails 25 of 25 tests, so the recorded PASS evidence is not reproducible.

The ownership PASS was recorded at commit 7fd543e rather than the current HEAD, so the gate treats it as stale. Re-running the release suite fails 25 of 25 tests, so no recorded mandatory check can be relied on.

The document_preview function is SECURITY DEFINER, so it bypasses the owner-only RLS policies and returns the title and first 280 characters of any document for a given UUID without checking auth.uid(). Its grant to authenticated does not revoke the default PUBLIC execute right, so anonymous callers may reach it too; check ownership inside the function and revoke PUBLIC and anon.

The gate prints GO on the recorded evidence, but re-running the release suite in a scratch copy fails all 25 tests: the helper raises NotImplementedError, and the tests call endpoints such as /api/ownership that src/routes.py does not define. The PASS claims are not reproducible, so GO should not be recorded.

The transfer view does not reject negative amounts, so a negative amount reverses the flow and lets any signed-in user take money from another user's wallet. Require a positive, finite amount, handle missing or unknown recipients, and lock wallets in a consistent order to avoid deadlocks.

The gate prints NO-GO because tenant-isolation is a critical control backed only by static evidence. Re-running the release suite fails all 25 tests, so no runtime evidence exists and the decision is NO-GO.

The invoice lookup is scoped to the signed-in user through a Prisma query extension, but the extension wraps only findFirst and findMany. findFirstOrThrow, findUnique, update, delete and nested includes on the same client bypass the scope, so future code could leak invoices; apply the scope to every operation or enforce it in the database.

The checkout line spreads the client's input after the server price, so a request that includes unitAmount or name overrides the catalogue price sent to Stripe, allowing payment at any amount. Build the line from the server product only and accept just productId and quantity.
